terms.gloss: sing or chant over and over
evidence: Cic. Brut. 75: carmina in epulīs esse cantitāta (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Augustine’s word for the children’s sing-song from the house next door at Milan (Conf. 8.12.29).
Usually of something trite, said over and over (Lewis & Short).
Chiefly a dirge (Cic., Hor.); Horace gives the name to the children’s chant of the king game.

phrases.latin: at puerī lūdentēs: «rēx eris» ajunt, «sī rēctē faciēs»
phrases.english: but the children in their game say, “You’ll be king if you do right”

phrases.latin: utrumnam solērent puerī in aliquō genere lūdendī cantitāre tāle aliquid
phrases.english: whether children used to chant anything like that in some game

sources: Lewis & Short: cantito · Lewis & Short: decanto · Lewis & Short: nenia
